decisions.summary: the pulled lane's clearance row re-tiered E2 and fixed (bdc9d5053): straighten_joints hands _one_joint the buildings (_BUILDINGS: houses, farm_sheds, byres, retirement_houses from _homestead_polys); a pull passes if _clear_link clears it at the usual margins against everything, or if _clear_link clears it against hard and walls with the buildings removed AND _clear_touch at g = max(4, w/2+2) clears it against the buildings alone AND every dropped vertex is within _JOG_FT (6 ft) of the new line
decisions.why: Round 2's item is met. 0081: 'keep its usual clearance from fences and buildings. It may come right up to the buildings when the straightened line stays within 6 ft of the old one.' The touch at g now reaches the buildings only; the crop, envelope, toe and marsh (hard, 8 ft) and the fences, groves, wells, wood seats, commons and fixtures (walls, 7 ft) keep _clear_link's usual margins, and the 6 ft condition rides only the touch branch. The exclusion is by exact polygon key and is sound: at web.py:600-627 hard_built's _solid and walls are both built from the same _homestead_polys(s) list straighten_joints reads, so a building's polygon is the same tuple in all three (seated parts, whose sheds carry another kind, are cleared at household_ways.py:124 before the web runs). The claim line ('all but the buildings keep the usual clearance ... a fence, a grove, a well, a fixture and the crop keep _clear_link's margins') and tasks.md Phase 39 now say what the code does. test_a_pull_may_touch_a_building_and_nothing_else (houses straightened, garden and well kept) passes on the clone (make test-file, 2026-10-08). The exception is now exactly the page's, so it is no longer a narrowing to rule on.

decisions.summary: farm fixtures (privy, manure heap, bath, coop, hokora) not counted among the buildings a pull may touch; they keep the usual 7 ft
decisions.why: 0081 licenses the touch for 'the buildings' and is otherwise the usual clearance; 0246's own enumeration ('houses, yards, beds, sheds, wells and fixtures are fabric a lane keeps off') lists fixtures as a class apart from houses and sheds, so withholding a permissive 'may' from them applies the page's rule as written rather than narrowing it (the tie goes to the page's default). Not a finding, one note for T102's impl-drift: the _BUILDINGS docstring glosses the buildings as 'the roofed fabric', which a privy, bath, coop and hokora also are - the reason is 0246's separate fixtures class, not roofing, and the line should say so (or label the boundary CONVENTION).
